title: Mushroom Picking Around Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Small amounts for your own pan are legal.** Berlin forest law and Brandenburg forest law both allow collecting mushrooms in small quantities for personal use. Selling what you pick is banned, and Brandenburg does not grant commercial permits for the state forest.

**Porcini and chanterelles are protected species with an exception.** The federal species ordinance lets you take Steinpilz, Pfifferling, Birkenpilz, Rotkappe and Brätling in small amounts for yourself. Bucket-scale picking is where the fines start.

**Signed nature reserves are off limits.** Inside a Naturschutzgebiet you stay on the path and pick nothing. The big state forests around them are open, so the honest move is simply to read the signs at the edge.

**The 2026 season is late.** The dry summer kept the forest floor quiet into September; the mycelium is alive and waiting. The season stands or falls with autumn rain, so go two to five days after a proper wet spell.

**Ten good forests sit on a normal VBB ticket.** Köpenicker Stadtforst is 33 minutes from Alexanderplatz on the S3, Grunewald 22 on the S7, the beeches of Chorin 54 on the RE3, the Liepnitzwald 56 via the RB27 Heidekrautbahn.

**A free expert will check your basket.** The Pilzberatung at the Botanical Garden, Botanikschule at Unter den Eichen 5, examines finds at no charge in season. Suspected poisoning: Giftnotruf 030 19240.
